newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares scrape to new closing high.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares scrape to new closing high.

text.p: Dutch shares squeaked to their fourth consecutive closing high of the week on Friday, bouncing up from a near 10 point fall after a solid Wall Street rise on the back of U.S. February jobs data.

"Wall Street was really helping us in the last half hour. The hourly earnings figure was extremely good and the picture of an economy that's growing but not overheating remains intact," said a dealer. "Every thing still seems under control."
The AEX index closed 0.29 points higher at 764.96 after earlier giving up most of Thursday's 9.44 gain to touch a session's low of 755.40. Volume was said to be fairly thin.
The market initially lunged to the day's low on the jobs figures which showed a bigger than expected rise in non-farm U.S. jobs but a smaller than anticipated rise in hourly pay.

Prices had been lower throughout the morning as profit-takers made their mark following a run which has brought the AEX up from 736 at the beginning of the week on a steady stream of strong Dutch company results and outlooks.

Dealers said prices had been additionally depressed early on by worries that the guilder's recent weakness against the mark might prompt another Dutch central bank interest rate tightening after last week's 20 basis point hike.

Dealers also said part of today's early decline was from disappointment with Wall Street yesterday. The Dow was up 25 points when Amsterdam finished on Thursday only to fade to a small loss by its own close.

Retailer Ahold picked up modestly from where it left off on Thursday, closing up 1.70 guilders at 139.10 for a two-day gain of 6.90 guilders following yesterday's news of a 39 percent surge in 1996 profits and forecast of 1997 earnings growth.
Aegon closed 3.90 guilders up at 132.90, squeezed by short covering. Other financials were mixed with ING up 40 cents to 77.90 guilders and ABN AMRO down 1.60 guilders to 138.60.
